title: Wabash–Ohio navigation-pool backwater boundary scenario
label: SIMULATION
purpose: Document testable boundary conditions for how a permanent Ohio River navigation pool may affect tributary (Wabash) outlet hydraulics and alluvial water-table head near Point Township. For digital-twin and FOIA scoping only.

navigation_dam.name: John T. Myers Locks and Dam
navigation_dam.role: run-of-river navigation pool (Commerce Clause / navigational servitude context)

mechanisms_hypothesis.summary: Gates establish Normal Pool / navigation pool elevating base water-surface relative to natural low-flow gradient.
Flattened mainstem slope acts as downstream boundary condition for Wabash outflow; tributary stage may stack during coincident high flow.
Sustained channel stage may raise head in connected alluvial aquifer, reducing unsaturated storage before storm events.
During major floods, movable dams may be operated open-river; residual impact hypothesis is pre-event saturation and geometry, not peak storage behind the dam.

required_inputs_before_any_filing: USACE pool elevation time series and gate/operation logs (FOIA)
Validated gage datums (NAVD88) for Ohio and Wabash stations
Surveyed LAG / EC by PE or RLS
Hydrogeologic data before asserting water-table rise magnitude
suggested_model_stages: Steady boundary: Ohio pool stage as downstream WSE

software_notes.preferred: HEC-RAS 2D or equivalent; results labeled SIMULATION_DEMO until PE-sealed
software_notes.tsm_planes: Scientific/Simulation plane only; Evidence plane records inputs/hashes; no auto governance action

references_public: USACE Louisville District — Myers Locks and Dam public project materials
USGS NWIS / NOAA NWPS stage products (gage height ≠ WSE_NAVD88 without validated zero)
